Thank you, this is the comment with the most consequence for the plan, and the links are new to me. The row you are on argues that a graph store should not become the text-search layer, and it sounds like the Orbit team reached the same conclusion from the other direction. The part I want to avoid is the obvious failure mode: two teams building code search at the same time. Before this document moves from proposed to accepted I would like a working session with the Orbit team and you, with a written split as the output: who owns the text index, who owns the graph, who owns the SCIP symbol store, and one request contract in front of both. The document already proposes a single SCIP symbol store with a single owning team consumed by both the plane and the graph, so that decision is on the table rather than being asserted here. One question that decides whether this is overlap or a layer: does orbit-next target the same scope this document does, meaning organization-wide, server-side, and permission-aware at the source of truth, or is it retrieval scoped to what an agent already has checked out? If it is the former, we should pick one and staff it. If it is the latter, the two compose and the contract is where they meet. I will add orbit-next and the knowledge-graph MR to the related work in the document either way, so the next reader finds them.

:robot: AI-generated > Could the wording here say "per module" explicitly to match ADR-007 and avoid the ambiguity? Done. The Go clause now reads "the cap applies per module path and counts every version name ever published for that module, deleted names included", which matches ADR-007's "stay bounded per module path" and no longer reads as a repository-wide cap.

:robot: AI-generated > Should a short note (e.g., "5 reserved for Debian") be added next to the enum so the gap is self-explanatory without needing the MR description? Done, in both places a reader would hit the gap. The ERD comment now reads `..., 4=generic, 5=debian (reserved), 6=go`, and the `repositories` bullet adds one clause after the format list: "Value `5` is reserved for the Debian format, which has its own amendment, so Go takes `6`." It only explains the reservation; Debian itself stays in its own amendment.

issue (blocking, process): our process for ADRs changed recently. An ADR now holds only the direction and the constraints it sets, the things that must always hold. It leaves out code identifiers, per-feature detail and step-by-step mechanics, which go to the spec. See the [flow table]([주소] and the [ADR template]([주소] Most of what this adds is detail that only applies to the new Go modules format, and your Reach answer is that one format, so it belongs in the Go modules spec (gitlab-org/ops/artifact-registry!3484). Could you add to the ADRs only what must always hold for Go modules, and put the rest in the spec? ADR-007 already has this level of detail for the other package formats, and there's no need to trim that here. Let's just not add more of it.
